Immersion grows through deliberate practice. A learner notices unfamiliar vocabulary while reading an engaging article, checks each meaning in context, and returns to the same ideas over several days. The routine should remain simple enough to repeat: read a paragraph, capture useful terms, reveal an answer, rate the memory honestly, and continue. Local software can support that rhythm without sending private reading material to a server. A compact dictionary resolves common inflections, while a scheduler records when each card should appear again. Reliable persistence matters because progress should survive a browser restart, and coordination matters because a second tab must not overwrite a review performed in the first. Good tools stay quiet during focused reading. They preserve the source sentence, show a concise definition and pronunciation, and make the next action obvious. Over time, repeated encounters turn uncertain words into familiar language, allowing attention to return from dictionary mechanics to the argument, story, or technical explanation that made the text worth reading in the first place.
